scope: Possible editorial angles, not extra facts. Use only the evidence packet and reject any angle it does not support.

signal.angle: What is being demonstrated is not just answering a question, but completing a complex task through a workflow. Explain the concrete shared emphasis in Google and Anthropic announcements without treating their architectures as identical or claiming broad adoption.

structure.angle: Explain the division of work among humans who define a goal/acceptance test, models that propose work, and tools that check a result. Antigravity and AlphaProof Code illustrate different checking mechanisms; the BCI study illustrates why real-world testing has different limits. Do not call different checking methods equivalent or say human work has been eliminated.

consequence.angle: A useful cross-field question is how researchers choose what to try next before expensive experiments or simulations. AlphaGenome, the sodium-ion design rule, and climate-emulator training are different technologies, not all AI applications. Describe possible changes to screening/experiment choice/model-building, not proven medical benefit, cheaper commercial batteries, quantified cost savings or better global forecasts.
consequence.boundary: The sodium-ion paper was published earlier; the November 14 date belongs to this selection's media coverage. Say this issue reports or describes the study, not that the invention happened this week.

limits: This is an interpretation of an editorially selected set of announcements and research reports. It cannot establish industry-wide momentum, independent replication or product/clinical readiness. Do not force the NVIDIA leadership transition into a technological trend.
